FinTech Week concludes
body:
Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026 concluded today, capping a week of discussions, business exchanges, startup showcases and ecosystem activities that brought together policymakers, regulators, entrepreneurs, investors and innovators from around the world.

 

The week-long programme attracted more than 48,000 visitors from over 120 economies, featured over 1,100 speakers and 800 exhibitors, and welcomed more than 30 Chinese Mainland and international delegations.

 

The programme was organised by the Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau, the Commerce & Economic Development Bureau and Invest Hong Kong.

 

Throughout the week, speakers explored how financial and technological innovation are reshaping industries, business models and global markets. Artificial intelligence (AI) discussions highlighted both the expanding potential of the technology and the foundations needed to support wider adoption.

 

A key highlight of the week was the finale of Global Fast Track 2026, connecting startups and scale-ups with corporate leaders, investors and potential business partners. Following over 700 applications from more than 120 economies, selected finalists presented their solutions at the main conference.

 

More than 30 delegations from the Chinese Mainland, including those from Beijing, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Zhuhai, as well as delegations from North America, Europe, the Gulf Cooperation Council regions, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Central Asia, and other emerging markets, participated in conference sessions, ecosystem exchanges and business engagement activities throughout the week.

 

Beyond the main conference, participants took part in a series of community and partner events across the city, including investor meetings, startup showcases, networking sessions and ecosystem exchanges.

 

During the two-day Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Immersive Executive Tour to Shenzhen, participants visited leading technology enterprises covering AI, electric vehicles, fintech and robotics, gaining first-hand insights into one of the world's most dynamic innovation ecosystems.

title: CE attends import expo in Shanghai
body:
The ninth China International Import Expo is being held from today until November 10 at the National Exhibition & Convention Center in Shanghai, with Chief Executive John Lee attending the expo today.

 

A record high of over 400 Hong Kong enterprises are participating in this year's expo.

 

In the morning, Mr Lee attended the opening ceremony of the expo and the Hongqiao Forum. Later, he accompanied Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang in touring the Hong Kong exhibition area of the China Pavilion.

 

Under the theme “Connectivity & Enterprise”, the Hong Kong exhibition area showcases Hong Kong’s commitment to capitalising on its role as a bridge linking China and the world, and its multiple top rankings in global indexes.

 

Mr Lee attended the “Hong Kong Parallel Session” of the Hongqiao Forum in the afternoon. The session was jointly organised by the Hong Kong SAR Government and the Ministry of Commerce.

 

Mr Lee and Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao both delivered remarks at the session, while Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong also attended. Under the theme “Aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, Serving the National Development, & Seizing New Opportunities for Hong Kong”, the session attracted around 400 participants.

 

Mr Lee remarked that this was the first large-scale briefing session held at an international forum since the Hong Kong SAR Government announced Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, which laid out the city's unique advantages of being strongly supported by its motherland and closely connected to the world under the “one country, two systems” principle.

 

He said Hong Kong will continue to play its role as a “super connector” and “super value-adder”, advance its development of “four centres and one hub”, and contribute its strengths towards building a great country.

 

After the session, Mr Lee toured the Enterprise & Business Exhibition and showed support for Hong Kong enterprises at the Hong Kong Food Pavilion and Hong Kong Services Pavilion, both set up by the Trade Development Council.

 

Together, the two pavilions are hosting 71 Hong Kong enterprises, with over 60% of these exhibiting for the first time this year, showcasing quality Hong Kong products and services across sectors such as food, finance, professional services, logistics and transportation, and innovation and technology (I&T).

 

Invest Hong Kong and the Tourism Board are also using the expo to promote Hong Kong’s advantages and its latest tourism offerings.

 

In the evening, Mr Lee hosted a networking dinner, where he exchanged views with political and business leaders from Hong Kong and the Mainland. He promoted Hong Kong's professional services and I&T sectors, and encouraged Mainland enterprises to make use of the city as a platform to “go global”.

title: CE promotes Beijing-HK ties
body:
Continuing a visit to Beijing, Chief Executive John Lee attended the opening ceremony of the 29th Beijing-Hong Kong Economic Cooperation Symposium this morning.

 

This year's edition of the event is themed “Beijing-Hong Kong: Together into the 15th Five Year Plan”.

 

In a speech at the ceremony, Mr Lee remarked that the symposium has achieved fruitful results over nearly three decades, during which time co-operation between Beijing and Hong Kong has gradually expanded from trade, commerce and infrastructure to high-end areas such as financial services, innovation and technology, green and low-carbon development, intellectual property and professional services.

 

He added that by putting Hong Kong’s international resources at the service of Beijing’s high-quality development, and opening up channels for Beijing’s innovative industries to go global, the symposium has promoted two-way investment and joint development, and played an important role in deepening Beijing-Hong Kong collaboration.

 

Mr Lee said Beijing and Hong Kong can further deepen collaboration in three main directions in the future.

 

These include advancing two-way financial opening-up, where Hong Kong, as the most convenient international financing platform for Beijing enterprises, joins hands with Beijing to expand green finance and offshore renminbi business.

 

Another direction, he said, involves deepening collaboration in innovation and technology, accelerating the development of the Northern Metropolis and building an internationalised university town to promote the integrated development of education, technology and talent. It also entails a new chapter for Beijing and Hong Kong institutions in jointly nurturing high-calibre talent and fostering new quality productive forces.

 

Mr Lee also highlighted the direction of giving full play to Hong Kong’s roles as a “super connector” and a “super value-adder” to fully empower enterprises in "going global", thereby helping to bring Chinese culture and soft power to the world.

 

The Chief Executive said Hong Kong will continue to proactively serve the country’s needs and work with Beijing to transform co-operation between the two places into a new impetus of high-quality development, contributing to the country’s high-standard opening up.

 

Mr Lee later departed for Shanghai to attend a welcome dinner for the Ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) and took the opportunity to exchange views with participants from all over the world.

title: Commerce chief joins APEC e-meet
body:
Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau attended the video conference of the 37th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) ministerial meeting yesterday evening.

 

The theme for APEC this year is “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together”.

 

During a discussion session, Mr Yau emphasised that member economies must collaborate together through enhanced dialogue and co-operation to achieve shared prosperity amid rapidly evolving global landscape and technological advancements.

 

Citing digital transformation as an example, Mr Yau said that practical co-operation is essential for member economies to harness their respective strengths in digital technologies in a people-centred and inclusive manner. He added that Hong Kong is strengthening its research capacity in frontier technologies and launching programmes to promote public awareness and the responsible use of AI.

 

He urged member economies to continue to strengthen connectivity across various areas to enable the efficient flow of goods, services, capital and people, while narrowing development gaps and creating opportunities region-wide. He added that collaborative efforts among member economies should continue to be guided by the Putrajaya Vision 2040 and the Aotearoa Plan of Action.

 

At another discussion session, Mr Yau noted that enhancing economic integration remains a core objective of APEC, with advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) as a direction.

 

“As part of Hong Kong's wider efforts to contribute to the FTAAP agenda, we have been actively seeking early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership. We welcome the establishment of the Accession Working Group for Hong Kong in September this year, and hope that our accession could inject fresh impetus into advancing the FTAAP agenda,” he said.

 

Mr Yau also highlighted the importance of enhancing co-operation to deal with the seismic changes in the trade landscape. As technological advancement increasingly transforms international trade, deepening co-operation in this area is vital for promoting cross-boundary trade and investment. He stated that Hong Kong fully supports the proposed Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework as a guiding document for future co-operation.

 

He stressed that the multilateral trading system must remain the foundation of regional integration and international trade.

 

“We call on member economies to continue supporting the World Trade Organization (WTO)'s reform agenda, incorporating plurilateral initiatives into the WTO framework, finding a permanent solution for the moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, and facilitating the Work Programme on Electronic Commerce,” he said.

title: LawTech funding scheme launched
body:
The Department of Justice (DoJ) today officially launched the Funding Scheme for LawTech Solution Subscription by the Hong Kong Legal Sector, aiming to boost the local legal sector’s technological capability and fortify the city’s status as an international legal and dispute resolution hub.

 

The scheme is a policy initiative under the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address. It will be jointly managed by the Hong Kong Bar Association and the Law Society of Hong Kong, which will handle applications and disburse funds.  

 

Applications are open from today until January 29, 2027. Eligible applicants include sole practitioners, Hong Kong law firms with no more than five partners, and barristers with no more than seven years of call.

 

Deputy Secretary for Justice and Chairman of the Consultation Group on LawTech Development Cheung Kwok-kwan stated that promoting LawTech is a core DoJ policy initiative. He noted that since last year, the DoJ has hosted five rounds of the LexGoTech Roundtables to gather feedback from practitioners, academics and stakeholders.

 

He added that the DoJ is aware that small and medium-sized law firms, as well as junior barristers, are particularly concerned about the financial burden of adopting LawTech tools. The scheme is launched to directly respond to the industry’s needs.

 

He pointed out that small and medium-sized law firms account for about 88% of all law firms in Hong Kong, while junior barristers with less than seven years of call make up about one-third of the total practicing bar. The scheme will lower the barrier to entry and enhance the overall competitiveness of Hong Kong's legal sector.

 

Operating on an actual-expense reimbursement basis, the scheme provides up to $20,000 per applicant for a one-year subscription. Applicants can choose from a designated list of 14 local, Mainland and overseas providers covering legal research, document drafting, workflow management and hearing support.

 

To ensure effectiveness, these service providers will offer transparent pricing alongside technical support and training. The application process consists of four steps.

 

First, applicants must select a provider from the designated list and obtain a written price quotation. Second, they will submit their application to either the Hong Kong Bar Association or the Law Society of Hong Kong.

 

Third, the relevant body will issue a written result, after which successful applicants can subscribe to their chosen service. Finally, applicants submit proof of subscription and payment to their respective professional body to claim reimbursement.

Northern Link Project pact signed
body:
With the Chief Executive in Council approving the financial arrangement for Part 2 of the Northern Link (NOL) Project today, the Government and the MTR Corporation (MTRC) have executed the agreement for the full NOL Project.

 

Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan and the MTRC Chairman Jacob Kim witnessed the representatives of the Transport & Logistics Bureau and the MTRC signing the agreement.

 

The milestone indicates that the NOL Main Line and Spur Line have fully entered the construction stage, targeting a simultaneous commissioning by 2034 or sooner.

 

Ms Chan noted that the venture is a strategic railway project under Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, actively aligning with the strategies set out in the National 15th Five-Year Plan Outline.

 

Providing local commuting alongside cross-boundary railway services, the project will open up new transport corridors for both domestic and cross-boundary transit upon its full rollout. 

 

Ms Chan said the project features three highlights - serving the Northern Metropolis, joining two lines, and linking the Greater Bay Area.

 

“First, the project will serve as the main public transport backbone for several new development areas in the Northern Metropolis including the innovation and technology clusters in the San Tin Technopole and the Loop, driving the expedited development of the Northern Metropolis.

 

“Secondly, the project will link the Tuen Ma Line and the East Rail Line to form a railway loop, significantly enhancing the coverage and resilience of the railway network.

 

“Thirdly, the project will connect to the Huanggang Port, thereby integrating the metro networks of Hong Kong and Shenzhen and strengthening infrastructure interconnectivity in the Greater Bay Area.”

 

To enhance the speed and efficiency of railway development, over the past year the Government and the MTRC teams have taken forward a series of key initiatives to reduce cost and expedite construction.

 

Ms Chan highlighted that the time for handling building plans has been reduced by 30 to 50%. By implementing the NOL Main Line in combination with the Spur Line as one project, it will also advance the timetable of the Spur Line by two years to commission simultaneously with the Main Line by 2034 or earlier.

 

The estimated capital cost is verified to be about $54.8 billion. Together with the estimated capital cost for Part 1, the estimated capital cost of the entire NOL Project is about $86.2 billion, which is lower than the original estimate by 28%.

 

The Chief Executive in Council also approved the grant of sites at Ngau Tam Mei Area 3A, 3D and 4A; San Tin Area 2A and 2G; Kwu Tung North Area 23 and 26 (East); as well as part of the site for residential use in the proposed Au Tau New Development Area, to the MTRC for residential and commercial development under the "Rail-plus-Property" model.

 

The NOL Main Line involves the construction of a 10.7-kilometre-long underground railway and five stations. There will be two interchange stations at Kam Sheung Road Station and Kwu Tung Station connecting with the Tuen Ma Line and the East Rail Line respectively, as well as three intermediate stations at San Tin, Ngau Tam Mei and Au Tau.

 

Upon commissioning, the travelling time between Kam Sheung Road and Kwu Tung during peak hours will be significantly reduced from the current 60 minutes to 12 minutes.

 

The Spur Line involves the construction of an underground railway of about 6 kilometres in length branching off from San Tin Station on the NOL Main Line, of which the Shenzhen section is approximately 1.1 kilometres long.

 

There will be three new stations, including intermediate stations at Chau Tau and the Loop, as well as the terminal at the Huanggang Port in Shenzhen. The travelling time between San Tin and the Huanggang Port is expected to be only about 11 minutes upon commissioning.

title: HK 11th on digital competitiveness
body:
Hong Kong has been ranked 11th globally and fourth in Asia in the World Digital & AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026 index, published by the International Institute for Management Development (IMD).

 

Among the five factors under consideration, Hong Kong ranks inside the top 10 for workforce development, efficiency, and technology and infrastructure.

 

In terms of sub-factors, Hong Kong ranks top on technological framework (under technology and infrastructure), practices (under efficiency), and education and training (under workforce development). It also ranks inside the top 10 on talent (under workforce development), societal attitudes (under values) and regulatory framework (under governance).

 

The Government said that WDAIR 2026 recognises Hong Kong as one of the world’s most competitive economies for digital and AI development. It highlighted that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan sets out a vision for the city’s development as an international centre for innovation and technology, one that has the full backing of the central authorities.

 

It iterated that Hong Kong will foster new industrialisation with regard for local circumstances, advance the Artificial Intelligence+ Initiative on all fronts, enhance computing infrastructure, support small-and-medium-sized enterprises in their adoption of AI, and empower different sectors of the economy through AI technology.

 

In terms of upstream research, the Government will build on the “dual base” advantages of the city’s InnoHK Research Clusters and State Key Laboratories, and advance the development of the Hong Kong Microelectronics Research & Development Institute, the Hong Kong Artificial Intelligence Research & Development Institute and the Life & Health Technology Research Institute.

 

Meanwhile, the Government will accelerate the development of national strategic emerging industries and foster new quality productive forces, including through establishing Hong Kong’s first national manufacturing innovation centre.

 

It will also enhance the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem on multiple dimensions, including computing power, funding and risk management. Construction of the Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster is underway and the cluster is expected to be fully operational by 2032 or earlier, providing computing power of 180,000 peta-floating point operations per second, equivalent to 36 times Hong Kong’s current computing power.

 

The Government has also launched an AI Subsidy Scheme to support the industry in using high-performance computing power for frontier research, and is optimising the Digital Transformation Support Pilot Programme to provide matching subsidies to support more small and medium enterprises in applying AI and cybersecurity solutions.

 

In addition, the Government will continue to build digitally-led public services. The “iAM Smart” platform has achieved the goal of a single portal for online government services, with daily usage exceeding 220,000 interactions. The platform provides access to more than 1,400 online services.

 

Meanwhile, the AI Efficacy Enhancement Team is driving government departments to apply AI technology. It has so far facilitated 30 projects involving 13 departments.

 

Going forward, the Government will aim to promote closer collaboration with the industrial, academic, research and investment sectors, consolidate and enhance Hong Kong’s competitive edge in the global market, and provide more convenient, efficient and reliable public services.

title: Robot loan applications open
body:
The Digital Policy Office (DPO) today announced that applications are now open for the "Robots in the Community" Pilot Programme, allowing eligible organisations to borrow robots for demonstrations and performances at free community events. Applications are free of charge and will close on November 20.

 

By loaning a humanoid robot named "Smart Bot" at no cost for events hosted by community groups, the scheme enables the public to interact with it first-hand. This direct engagement aims to enhance public understanding of embodied artificial intelligence (AI).

 

Eligible applicants include Hong Kong companies, societies, district organisations, welfare agencies, and Legislative Council or District Council members' offices that serve the public or local residents. Proposed community events under this application round must take place between December 15, 2026, and February 28, 2027.

 

At these events, "Smart Bot" can perform dancing and kung fu. It can also act as a popular science ambassador to share knowledge of embodied AI and other digital technologies with participants.

 

The DPO has introduced various initiatives under the "Smart Silver" Digital Inclusion Programme to assist people in need, particularly the elderly, understand and use digital products and services. The "Robots in the Community" Pilot Programme will be the latest addition to this campaign.
